result.dimension: core encode/decode semantics and control flow of the script

findings.rule: CONTROL FLOW / LINE ORDER. Up to 4 lines are printed to stdout, always in this fixed order, each terminated by \n (including the last), stdout encoding is UTF-8. Exit code is ALWAYS 0 once argparse succeeds (no exception escapes). Lines: (1) ENCODE line — printed iff mode in {encode, both}: either `b'<ascii>'` (Python bytes repr of idna.encode(domain, strict)) or `encode_error: <msg>`. (2) ULABEL line — printed iff mode in {encode,both} AND first_label != '' AND encode of the WHOLE domain succeeded AND idna.ulabel(idna.encode(first_label, strict)) does not raise ANYTHING (bare `except: pass`). (3) DECODE line — printed iff mode in {decode, both}: either the decoded unicode domain or `decode_error: <msg>`. (4) LENGTH line — printed iff first_label != '' : literally `True` or `False` (Python bool str). first_label = domain.split('.')[0] using ONLY U+002E, regardless of --strict.

findings.rule: LABEL SEPARATORS. When strict is FALSE, both idna.encode and idna.decode split the domain on the regex character class [.。．｡] — EXACTLY four characters: '.' Alt separators also set the trailing-dot flag.

findings.rule: THE <repr> IN ERROR MESSAGES IS PYTHON'S repr() OF THE str LABEL. Rules to reproduce in Node: prefer single quotes; if the string contains a single quote AND no double quote, wrap in double quotes; if it contains both, wrap in single quotes and backslash-escape the single quotes. Escape backslash as \\, \n, \t, \r; other non-printable/unassigned codepoints as \xNN (< U+0100), \uNNNN (BMP), \UNNNNNNNN (astral). Printable non-ASCII (letters, emoji) is emitted RAW as UTF-8. Position N is 1-based within the label.

Message (F) 'Label ends with illegal codepoint directionality' has two source sites (RFC 5893 rules 3 and 6) but only the RTL one (rule 3) is reachable through this program; I could not construct any input that reaches the LTR variant. If some exotic codepoint exists with bidi class R/AL/AN that is somehow skipped by the rule-5 check, that conclusion would change — none was found.

Whether check_bidi is ever invoked with check_ltr=True anywhere in the bundled idna (which would make rule 6 reachable and would also make pure-LTR labels subject to rules 1/5/6) could not be observed; every probe is consistent with check_ltr=False everywhere.
